When are Americans driving?

On an average weekday, the share of Americans driving peaks at 5:00 PM, when 11.6% of people age 15 and older (about 29.2 million) are driving. On weekends it peaks at 12:00 PM (7.7%). Averaged over all days, Americans spend 50 min a day driving.

What it includes

Average time per weekday, for the activities in this group that take the most time.

  • Driving · Travel related to working: 16 min a day
  • Driving · Travel related to shopping (except grocery shopping): 7 min a day
  • Driving · Travel related to caring for and helping household children: 4 min a day
  • Driving · Travel related to eating and drinking: 3 min a day
  • Driving · Travel related to socializing and communicating: 3 min a day
  • Driving · Travel related to grocery shopping: 2 min a day
  • Driving · Travel related to caring for and helping nonhousehold adults: 2 min a day
  • Driving · Travel related to household activities: 2 min a day

About these numbers

Estimates come from all 258,954 diaries in the American Time Use Survey (Bureau of Labor Statistics and Census Bureau), 2003–2025, weighted to the U.S. civilian population age 15 and older and pooled across years. Times are local clock time. Counts are people on an average day of that type, not a live count. Weekdays are Monday–Friday. How the estimates work.
